title: Platform systems & services — runbooks, dashboards, and roadmap (Team Wiki)
author: Priya Patel
body:
Overview

This page is the canonical team wiki for Platform Systems & Services. It consolidates: inventories of services we operate, how-to guides for common platform tasks, the dashboards & alerting standards we follow, runbooks for high-impact incidents, recent retrospectives, and the 12-18 month roadmap. Use this as the single source of truth for day-to-day platform operations and for onboarding new team members.

Scope

- Applies to all systems owned by the Platform team: controller API, routing-service, batch-queue, autoscaler, KV-cache, model-router, metrics-collector, and internal tooling (deploy-bot, config-service).
- Does NOT replace team-level service READMEs. This page links to them and provides cross-cutting operational patterns.

Ownership and on-call

- Primary owner: Platform Systems (team).
- Service owners: see the Service Inventory section below for per-service pager/contact routing.
- On-call rotation: platform-oncall (PagerDuty) — escalation policy: 0-10m alert -> primary; 10-30m -> secondary; 30m+ -> SRE lead.

Service inventory (summary)

| Service | Responsibility | SLO (p99) | Primary Pager | Runbook link |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| controller-api | API surface for customer routing + auth | 99.9% availability | @controller-oncall | /confluence/eng-platform/controller-api-runbook |
| routing-service | Real-time request routing and policy engine | 99.5% latency < 200ms | @routing-oncall | /confluence/eng-platform/routing-service-runbook |
| autoscaler | Scale pools (Dedicated) | 95% success within 90s | @autoscaler-oncall | /confluence/eng-platform/autoscaler-runbook |
| kv-cache | Prefix/KV cache service | 99.9% availability | @cache-oncall | /confluence/eng-platform/kv-cache-runbook |
| batch-queue | Offline batching for embeddings | Throughput 200 reqs/s | @batch-oncall | /confluence/eng-platform/batch-queue-runbook |

Dashboards & observability standards

Goals: fast incident TTR, clear owner assignment, and cost transparency.

1) Primary dashboards (Grafana) — one per service:
- Service Health (availability, error-rate, latency p50/p95/p99)
- Capacity (GPU/CPU/memory utilization, queue depth)
- Cost & tokens (estimated token-cost per-hour, batching efficiency)
- Deployment & rollout (active deploys, canary percentage)

2) Dashboard conventions:
- Title prefix: [svc] {service-name} — {view} (e.g., [svc] routing-service — Health)
- Time-range defaults: 1h / 6h / 24h
- Panel thresholds: green/yellow/red with clear numeric thresholds in panel description.
- Ownership label: include 'owner' as a dashboard variable in the top-right noting team and PD contact.

3) Metrics & tagging standards:
- All services MUST expose the following metric names: svc_request_total, svc_request_errors_total, svc_request_latency_seconds_bucket, svc_cpu_seconds_total.
- Add labels: service_name, environment, model_variant (when applicable), customer_tier.

Alerting policy and runbook linkage

Alerting principles: be precise, actionable, and avoid noisy alerts. Every alert MUST include: symptom, affected service(s), severity, runbook link, and suggested immediate action.

Alert tiers (examples):
- P0 (sev=critical): service unavailable (>=2 regions) OR p99 latency > 5x SLO for 15m. PagerDuty: page all.
- P1 (major): degraded service in a single region OR increase in error-rate > 5% absolute for 10m. PagerDuty: page primary.
- P2 (minor): capacity approaching threshold (85% sustained for 15m) OR cost spikes > 2x baseline. Notify in #platform-ops.

Example alert definition (Prometheus-style YAML snippet):

```
- alert: ControllerAPIHighErrors
  expr: rate(svc_request_errors_total{service_name=\"controller-api\"}[5m]) > 0.05
  for: 10m
  labels:
    severity: P1
  annotations:
    summary: \"High error rate on controller-api\"
    runbook: \"https://confluence.internal/redwood/eng-platform/controller-api-runbook\"
```

Runbooks (how to use them)

- Location: each runbook lives under /confluence/eng-platform/{service}-runbook and is linked from dashboards and alert annotations.
- Structure: summary, quick triage checklist, common remediation steps, rollback steps, post-incident tasks, owners.

Triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
1. Confirm alert: check Grafana panel + Prometheus query.
2. Check deploy history: `deploy-bot status --service {svc}` and recent git commits to main.
3. Identify scope: single region vs global, customer impact, request rate change.
4. If degraded: engage primary on-call and follow immediate mitigation (scale pool, apply config rollback, enable fallback model variant).

Common remediation patterns
- Scale up capacity: `kubectl -n platform scale statefulset autoscaler --replicas=3` (example; runbook contains exact commands per service).
- Enable fallback model: update routing config: `curl -X POST $CFG_SVC/api/v1/fallbacks -d '{\"service\":\"routing\", \"variant\":\"quantized-v1\"}'`
- Re-route traffic: update Envoy config via deploy-bot or run temporary traffic-split rule in routing-service.

Incident retrospective cadence

- All P0/P1 incidents require a blameless postmortem within 7 business days.
- Template fields: incident summary, timeline, root cause, mitigations applied, follow-ups, action owner, due date.
- Quarterly reliability review: aggregate incidents and surface systemic issues (e.g., autoscaling tuning, batching inefficiencies).

Recent retrospectives (high-level)

- Q4 2026 — Autoscaler oscillation: root cause was aggressive scaling policy + mismatch in observed CPU metrics. Fixes: introduced smoothing window and backoff; improvement: 42% reduction in flapping events.
- Jan 2027 — Controller API throttling during large rollout: root cause was rollout policy lacking exponential ramp. Fix: require canary window > 15 minutes and automatic rollback on error-rate delta > 3%.

Runbook examples (condensed) — routing-service outage

1) Signs: 50% increase in 5xx errors, p99 latency > 1s, queue_depth > 500.
2) Immediate actions (first 5m):
   a) Add capacity: `k8s scale deployment routing-service --replicas +2`
   b) Activate degraded mode: post to config-service to enable \"graceful-drop\" for non-critical customers.
   c) Notify customers: use status page template and #platform-ops.
3) Mitigation (5-30m):
   a) Identify slow downstream (kv-cache or model-router) and either restart pods with healthcheck or apply temporary route to backup region.
   b) If caused by a recent deploy: rollback to previous revision using `deploy-bot rollback --service routing-service`
4) Post-incident: create postmortem, schedule follow-ups, update runbook if any steps were unclear.

Roadmap (12-18 months)

Themes and major initiatives:
- Reliability & SLOs (Q2-Q3 2027): automated SLO regression alerting, tighter deploy safety checks, improved chaos test coverage.
- Observability & cost (Q3-Q4 2027): token-level cost attribution, automated cost-anomaly detection, dashboards for per-customer inference spend.
- Scaling & efficiency (Q4 2027-Q1 2028): GPU bin-packing improvements, autoscaler rewrite with ML-based predictions, KV-cache horizontal sharding.
- Developer productivity (ongoing): standardized service templates, improved local dev tooling, runbook-driven run-local scripts.

Roadmap milestones (high-level):
- 2027-04: Launch SLO regression monitor (beta).
- 2027-07: Deploy new autoscaler v2 to staging; benchmark throughput improvements.
- 2027-10: Roll out token-cost dashboards to account owners (pilot).
- 2028-01: KV-cache sharding alpha with live canary.

Onboarding & team wiki guidance

- New engineer checklist (platform systems):
  1. Get access: GitHub, PagerDuty, Grafana, Kibana, deploy-bot.
  2. Read core runbooks: controller-api, routing-service, autoscaler.
  3. Shadow on-call for two rotations.
  4. Complete the Platform 30-day project: own a small dashboard + runbook improvement PR.

- Useful links:
  - Grafana (primary dashboards): https://grafana.internal.redwood/
  - Prometheus: https://prometheus.internal.redwood/
  - PagerDuty: https://pagerduty.com/redwood
  - Deploy-bot docs: /confluence/eng-platform/deploy-bot-usage

Maintenance and housekeeping

- Dashboards must be reviewed quarterly by owners. Out-of-date dashboards are archived after 90 days of no changes.
- Alerts must be reviewed monthly in the Platform ops weekly: unnecessary alerts are retired or re-tuned.
- Runbook ownership must be confirmed on a quarterly roster; unclaimed runbooks are assigned to the Platform oncall lead.

Appendix: small snippets and checklists

- Quick grep for recent errors: `kubectl -n platform logs -l app={svc} --since=1h | grep ERROR | head -n 50`
- Promote canary: `deploy-bot promote --service {svc} --to=production --reason=\"canary passed\"`
- Emergency GCP project lock: contact infra-security@redwood.com (see security-and-compliance/access-and-permissions for process)

If anything on this page is unclear or you need additional runbooks added, file a request in #platform-ops or open a PR against this wiki page.
